top_choice_rationale: P001, Mircea Cărtărescu as sole laureate, is the only proposal that names a writer, and it is the proposal I judge best on the common criteria. The voice is distinctive and recognisable in long, densely patterned prose. On public knowledge of Blinding (the first part of the Orbitor trilogy) and Solenoid, the formal achievement lies in large architectures where recurring images and structures carry meaning. The intellectual depth comes from joining memory, the body and dream with cosmological speculation and twentieth-century Romanian history. The poetic origin and the essays suggest an oeuvre, not a single book, but I rely mainly on the large prose and treat the poetry as context. The citation should name the Romanian language and the volumes it leans on, so that it does not imply a claim for the translations or a full reading. Two reservations remain unresolved. We do not know whether the late, very large volumes deepen the project or repeat its motifs, and translation only partly conveys the rhythm and syntax of the long Romanian sentences. These limit how much the citation can claim. They do not show a failure of sustained quality, so I see no merit ground to prefer no award (P000). I do not treat the unanimity of the proposal slate as evidence of merit. This rests on public knowledge and not on fresh reading or independent verification, and it models a committee recommendation, not the decision of the full Swedish Academy.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile. My work on Selma Lagerlöf and my own fiction are context, not evidence of favoring this writer. The profile records no personal, institutional or translation connection to Mircea Cărtărescu.
